independent_computation.step_1_template_semantics: The only numeric split in Bloodsong's cached text is {{rd|8%|5%}}. Calibrating the rd template from inside the same cache: Hullbreaker writes its second argument literally as {{ap|120*0.7}}% and {{ap|5*0.7}}% and 70*0.5 to 130*0.5 — i.e. arg2 is arg1 scaled down by the well-known ranged-user penalty. Tiamat's {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} is the canonical melee/ranged cleave split. Therefore {{rd|A|B}} = A for a MELEE item holder, B for a RANGED item holder. Bloodsong: Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken if the Bloodsong holder is melee, +5% if the holder is ranged.
independent_computation.step_2_amplifier_form: "causing them to take X% increased damage from all sources" is a damage-taken amplifier on the victim, applying to ALL sources — including damage dealt by allies of the Bloodsong holder. So a multiplier keyed onto the carry's damage events in a roster scenario is the right KIND of leaf: multiplier = 1 + X/100.
independent_computation.step_4_window_check: Expose Weakness lasts 4 seconds per proc with a 1.5 s cooldown that starts after the empowered attack, so a sustained roster fight can legitimately carry the multiplier on a long run of consecutive damage events (an events[37] hit being amplified is not per se anomalous). Nothing in docs/math-foundations.md constrains this leaf: it documents resistance/penetration composition (§2) and expectation/renewal machinery (§1), and contains no statement about damage-taken amplifiers or melee/ranged item splits.
independent_computation.step_5_old_value: The old state (<absent>) asserts that no Bloodsong amplification applies to that event. The cached text is unambiguous that a champion hit by the empowered attack takes increased damage from all sources for 4 s, so an absent multiplier on an event inside that window contradicts the source. <absent> cannot be the correct value once the proc is modelled.

verification_limits.unresolvable_from_permitted_evidence: The roster composition of scenario 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (specifically the ATTACK TYPE of the champion holding Bloodsong) lives in scripts/golden_baseline.json / src/, which this runbook forbids reading. data/ contains no definition of this scenario: data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json has 22 scenarios and none references Bloodsong or Black Cleaver; data/worklists and data/champion-audit mention rosters only generically.
verification_limits.consequence: 1.08 is exactly the sourced MELEE branch. It is correct iff the Bloodsong holder in this scenario is a melee champion. If the holder is ranged, the sourced value is 1.05 and the leaf would be an 8%-vs-5% overstatement of every amplified event.
verification_limits.follow_up_check_for_the_implementer: Confirm the emitter conditions the multiplier on the Bloodsong holder's attack type (champions.json attackType / attack range), rather than hardcoding the melee 8%. A hardcoded 1.08 is a latent defect even where this scenario happens to be melee.

verdict_rationale: 1.08 = 1 + 8% is a genuinely sourced value from the cached wiki text (the melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}}), and the leaf's kind (a damage-taken amplifier applied to an ally's damage events, 'from all sources') matches the source exactly. The old value <absent> is affirmatively contradicted by the same text, so 'old_value_correct' is excluded. 'both_wrong' would require establishing that the Bloodsong holder is ranged, which the permitted evidence cannot show. Verdict is therefore new_value_correct, CONDITIONAL on the holder being melee — see verification_limits.
verdict_confidence: medium — the number is sourced and the semantics check out; the melee/ranged conditioning could not be verified from data/ alone.
